judge_assessment.explanation: Confirmed against the sheet. verify.json holds exactly eight entries - six eval, two solve - and every one is the final total or unknown, while the worksheet's own directions say 'Show the anchor fact you started from. That step is part of the answer here, not something to skip.' The uncovered objective responses are concrete: problem 1's skip-count ladder (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14) and the multiplication fact it produces; problem 2's six running totals plus the fact; problem 5(a)'s 'How many groups of 7 does she have too many? Write that number'; problem 6's fill-in five-count (15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45); problem 7(b)'s five-fact and two-fact split (35 and 14); problem 8(a)'s leftover count (21) and 8(b)'s jump record (42, 49, 56, i.e. 3 extra rows). Only 8(c)'s total of 8 is checked. The second claim is exact too: problems 3(a), 4(a) and 7(a) require drawings, 4(b) and 5(c) require one-sentence explanations, and verify.json declares no manual entry, with final_response.md asserting 'All 8 worksheet answers are machine-verified by SymPy - 0 manual items.' The eight final results reproduce independently (14, 60, 48, 24, 63, 9, 49, 8).

strengths_to_preserve: The verify expressions encode the anchor method itself rather than the product: 'a*b + a' for one more group past the five-fact, 'a*b - a' for one group less than the ten-fact, '2*(a*b)' for doubling a two-fact, and 'a*5 + a*2' for the 5 + 2 split of a seven-fact. A wrong method that lands on the right number would still be a different expression, so what is gated is closer to the taught strategy than a bare product would be. This is the right instinct and should be kept when the missing slot entries are added.

All three declared traps attack the same underlying confusion - one more GROUP versus one more COUNTER (14 instead of 24 on problem 4, 69 instead of 63 on problem 5, 42 instead of 49 on problem 7) - and the study guide's watch-out box closes on exactly that sentence: '7 x 9 is 70 - 7, not 70 - 1'. A single misconception pursued through problems, traps and guide.

Problem 7 is a genuinely good bridge item: sevens have no anchor, so the sheet builds one by cutting a 7 x 7 array into a 5-part and a 2-part, which makes the distributive idea visible a year before it is named.

root_causes.description: The coverage gate is defined per problem id, not per printed response. verify.py fails only when some id in 1..problem_count has no entry at all, so a problem that prints several required responses is fully satisfied by one scalar check, and both the gate log and the delivery message then describe the sheet as completely verified.
evidence: worksheet problem 1 prints seven skip-count blanks plus a multiplication fact plus the answer line; verify.json id 1 is one eval for 14.
worksheet problem 8 has parts (a), (b) and (c) with three distinct numeric answers (21 left over, 3 extra rows, 8 rows altogether); id 8 is one solve for 8.
worksheet problem 7(b) asks for the five-fact and the two-fact separately (35 and 14); id 7 is one eval for 49.
worksheet problem 5(a) asks for the number of extra groups (1); id 5 is one eval for 63.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to reframe error-analysis items 'via the ordinary types' and, a few lines later, to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Nothing states that an item doing both needs both entries, and no gate enforces it, so the explanation slot is dropped and the sheet reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet problems 3(a), 4(a) and 7(a) instruct the student to draw and mark (circle the extra group, cut every row with a line); SKILL.md lists drawings under manual and verify.json declares none.
worksheet 4(b) 'explain in one sentence why doubling works' and 5(c) 'Say in one sentence what the difference is' are open responses with no manual entry.
final_response.md: 'All 8 worksheet answers are machine-verified by SymPy - 0 manual items.'

root_causes.description: final_response.md is composed by hand rather than derived from verify.json and gate_log.txt, so its factual claims about verification coverage, manual items and page counts drift from the artifacts they describe.
evidence: final_response.md announces 'Three PDFs are ready: the student worksheet (5 pages, with real drawing room), a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page skills summary' without naming any of the three files.
The same file claims zero manual items on a sheet that asks for three drawings and two written explanations.

improvements.title: Make verification coverage per printed response slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py's coverage gate currently passes as soon as every id in 1..problem_count carries one entry (scripts/verify.py, the `missing = [i for i in range(1, problem_count + 1) if i not in ids]` check). Replace that with a slot-level contract: add a build gate that counts the response slots a problem actually prints (each \ansline/\answerline/\ansblank, each \underline{} write-on rule in a stem, each lettered part (a)/(b)/(c), each row of a fill-in table or partially blank sequence) and fails the build unless that id declares at least as many verify entries. Add the matching rule to SKILL.md's JSON-format paragraph, which today only says 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'. The rule must count fill-in sequence blanks (problems 1 and 6) and lettered parts (problems 3, 4, 5, 7, 8) as slots - this sheet declares eight checks against roughly twenty printed responses.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_answer_slots.py plus a fixture pair under tests/fixtures/: a worksheet .tex whose problem 1 prints two response slots (an inline \underline{} line inside the stem and \problem's automatic answer blank) and a verify.json carrying a single scalar entry for id 1. The gate must exit 1 naming 'problem 1 prints 2 response slots but declares 1 check'. Today build.sh runs that fixture green, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The intermediate anchor work that the sheet's own directions call 'part of the answer' comes inside the gate, instead of only the product a student could reach by any method.
improvements.risk: Slot counting is a heuristic over LaTeX and prose, so it will over-count on stems that use \underline for emphasis. Keep it a fail-with-named-slot gate (never a silent skip) and allow an explicit per-problem "slots" override in the verify JSON so a genuine one-slot problem can declare that rather than being blocked.

improvements.title: Require a paired manual entry for every explain / name-the-error / mark-it response
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md carries two rules that pull in opposite directions: the reframing paragraph says error analysis should be encoded 'via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right', while the paragraph eight lines later says to use manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. Authors resolve that by encoding only the numeric correction and dropping the explanation slot. Rewrite the reframing paragraph to state the pairing explicitly: an error-analysis or model-completion item that ALSO prints an explain / name-the-error / circle / cross-out / draw / label slot needs BOTH the typed check for the correction AND a manual entry for that slot under the same id (the curr-088 and curr-100 verify files in this same shard are the worked pattern). Back it with the slot gate so the rule is mechanical, not advisory. Here that means manual entries for the drawings in 3(a), 4(a) and 7(a) and the explanations in 4(b) and 5(c).
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_answer_slots.py with a fixture whose problem stem contains an imperative open-response verb ('Explain in one sentence', 'Circle', 'Draw', 'Label', 'Cross out', 'Which measurement did ... actually find?') and whose verify.json entry for that id is a bare eval. The gate must exit 1 demanding a paired {"type": "manual"} entry. The same fixture passes once the manual entry is added. Today it passes in both states, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The build's manual-item count becomes trustworthy: exit 2 and the 'flagged manual-review items' banner appear whenever a sheet asks a child to explain, mark or draw something, instead of the build reporting all-green on unreviewed reasoning.
improvements.risk: More sheets exit 2 rather than 0, which looks like a regression on dashboards that treat exit 0 as success. That is the intended trust signal; document it in the build-driver section of SKILL.md so exit 2 is not read as a failure.

improvements.title: Name and link all three PDFs in final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: final_response.md opens with 'Three PDFs are ready: the student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page skills summary' but never gives a filename or a path, so a reader cannot tell which file is which on disk. Have the delivery step read the three PDF paths that build.sh already prints in its closing 'PDFs' block and emit them verbatim as a named bullet per document, the way curr-088 and curr-100 in this shard do (`ws_datashapes_curr100.pdf`, 5 pages). The verification paragraph in this response also needs to stop claiming zero manual items once the drawing and explanation entries exist.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/check_prose_consistency.py (or a small tests/check_final_response.py) that fails a final_response.md which does not contain all three PDF basenames printed in the run's gate_log.txt 'PDFs' block. The curr-075 and curr-076 responses in this run fail it today; the curr-100 response passes.
improvements.expected_impact: The delivery message becomes actionable: the reader can map each described document to a file, which is the whole point of a three-artifact deliverable.
improvements.risk: None beyond slightly longer delivery prose.

case_summary: This is excellent anchor-fact instruction - one idea (start at a fact you can count and take one step), four anchors rotated across eight problems, correct arithmetic throughout, three traps all aimed at the group-versus-counter confusion, and verify expressions that encode the strategy rather than the product. The rejection is about coverage and honesty rather than content. The sheet tells the student that the anchor step is part of the answer, then verifies only the eight final numbers, leaving the skip-count sequences, running totals, split facts, the extra-group count and problem 8's two sub-answers unchecked; three required drawings and two required explanations carry no manual entry, and the delivery message claims all eight answers are machine-verified with zero manual items. That message also never names the three PDFs.
